_what_this_is: A LOCAL OVERRIDE. Copy this into {your-department-folder}/manager.json only when you want to change what the pack already declares. The pack's managers[] is the default and works untouched - you do not need this file to have a working manager.
_the_contract: A department is a MANAGER only if it has all three: owned state (one file answering 'what is the situation here'), a cadence (scheduled work that advances that state unprompted), and a gate (explicit publish authority per surface). Missing any one and it is a folder, not a manager. tools/lint_managers.py enforces this - it is code, not a suggestion.
_id_note: Logical key. Stable WITHIN your campus. NOT a product-wide constant - rename it if your business calls this something else.
_display_name_note: Cosmetic. Change this freely; nothing downstream notices. This is the ONLY layer a rename should touch.
_dept_dir_note: Your actual folder. It may be 'marketing/', 'departments/marketing/', 'marketing-manager/', or 'the-studio/' - whatever you actually named it. Nothing may assume dept_dir == id + '/'. On a clients or projects campus this folder may not exist at all, and that is fine: the staff org is separate from how you file finished work.
_shape_note: CLOSED enum: calendar | pipeline | roster | hybrid. Shapes describe HOW STATE MOVES, not what business you run. calendar = dated slots. pipeline = ordered stages with per-item aging. roster = people with per-person status. hybrid = a lifecycle that is both. A fifth shape is a kernel change and a version bump, not a config edit - so pick the closest fit rather than inventing one.
_state_file_note: A LITERAL path. Never write this as '{id}/something.md' and never let a consumer build it from the id - the first campus this shipped on has folders named '{dept}-manager/', so a derived path would have gone looking for a folder that does not exist on day one. Declare it; do not compute it.
_stale_note: A manager that stops advancing its state has stopped managing. This is how long silence is acceptable before the doctor says so.

cadence.advances: fills next week's open slots; queues production jobs

_cadence_note: enabled:false is the shipped default - recurring work costs money, so it switches on when YOU say so, not at install. model_tier: light|full. Planning may run light; voice-carrying copy and anything that publishes stay pinned full, always.

social._mode_note: auto = publishes without asking (requires a preflight). draft = writes, you send. owner_batch_gate = queues for one approval pass. dark = not this desk's surface at all.
social.preflight: Required for auto. Publish authority is permission to post, not permission to skip checks.

community.note: One desk owns a surface, never two.

buyer_defaults._locked: This MUST stay 'draft'. lint_managers.py treats anything else as an error. If you package your campus for someone else, their install ships all-draft-first regardless of what you grant yourself - they have not heard their own voice come back yet, and their first live post should be one they approved.
